hens_rule_text: Up to 5 chicken hens per single-family or multifamily dwelling, kept in the rear or backyard, with a city license.
permit_notes: A license from the city is required to keep chicken hens; the fee is $25 per hen, up to a maximum of $125 for 5 hens.
setback_notes: Coop or cage must be at least 20 ft from any door or window of a dwelling, school or church other than the keeper's own home; also at least 5 ft from a side lot line and 18 inches (5 ft in some cases) from a rear lot line, and not in the front or side street yard.
coop_rules: Total coop or cage area on a lot may not exceed 32 sq ft for up to 5 hens; must meet the code's design, location and sanitation standards.
zoning_notes: Multifamily properties such as duplexes need written consent from the owner and agreement of all tenants before keeping hens.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: City of Buffalo, NY, Code of Ordinances, Chapter 341 Property Maintenance
